simple.meaning: בָּלָה (bâlâh) is a Hebrew action word meaning “to fail ; by implication to wear out , decay (causatively, consume , spend ).” BibleIQ anchors the English reading to this source verb before comparing its uses.
simple.biblicalBackground: This action appears 16 times in Genesis, Deuteronomy, Joshua, 1 Chronicles, Nehemiah, and 4 more, beginning at Genesis 18:12. The surrounding contexts include wilderness, Israel.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to בָּלָה (H1086) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Actions in Scripture show what people do, what God does, and how covenant faithfulness or rebellion is described. BibleIQ compares the action across its occurrences.
simple.summary: בָּלָה (bâlâh) / H1086 is traced through Genesis 18:12, Deuteronomy 8:4, Deuteronomy 29:4, Joshua 9:13 with source-language evidence and verse context.

definitions.short: to fail ; by implication to wear out , decay (causatively, consume , spend )
definitions.usage: consume, enjoy long, become (make, wax) old, spend, waste.
definitions.full: H1086. balah [ בָּלָה ] verb become old and worn out (Arabic , Aramaic בְּלֵי , , Ethiopic id. ) — Qal Perfect בָּלְתָה Deut 8:4 , בָּלוּ 29:4 +; Imperfect יִבְלֶה Job 13:28 etc.; Infinitive with suffix בְּלֹתִי Gen 18:12 ; — wear out (intransitive), especially of garments Deut 8:4 ; 29:4 (twice in verse), all with מֵעַל pregnantly wear out (and fall) from upon... (hence Neh 9:21 ), Josh 9:13 ; figurative of the heavens (with simile of garment) Isa 50:9 ; Psa 102:27 יִבְלוּ כַּבֶּגֶד , the earth Isa 51:6 תִּבְלֶה כַּבֶּגֶד ; the bones (through suffering) Psa 32:3 ; afflicted man Job 13:28 יִבְלֶה כְּרָקָב וְהוּא (|| עָשׁ אֲכָלוֺ כְּבֶגֶד ); of an aged and decrepit woman Gen 18:12 (J) בְלֹתִי אַחֲרֵי after I am worn out. Pi`el causative of Qal. a. wear out (transitive), figurative Lam 3:4 וְעוֺרִי בְשָׂרִי בִּלָּה , Psa 49:15 and their form שְּׁאוֺל לְבַלּוֺת is for Sh®°ôl to consume away (others read לִבְלוֺת is for wasting away [Dr § 204 ], connecting ׳שׁ with following), 1Chr 17:9 לְבַלֹּתוֺ to wear it (Israel) out (altered from לְעַנּוֺתוֺ 2Sam 7:10 ), compare Dan 7:25 Aramaic b. wear out by use, use to the full , Isa 65:22 and the work of their hands יְבַלּוּ they shall use to the full, enjoy , Job 21:13 they wear out their days in prosperity (Qr here יְכַלּוּ complete , which perhaps is the true reading in both passages; compare Exod 5:13 ; Job 36:11 ). — On ַבּלּוֺתֹּי Psa 92:11 , see below בָּלַל .

occurrences.englishText: Sarah laughed within herself, saying, “After I have grown old will I have pleasure, my lord being old also?”
Your clothing didn’t grow old on you, neither did your foot swell, these forty years.
But Yahweh has not given you a heart to know, eyes to see, and ears to hear, to this day.
But Yahweh has not given you a heart to know, eyes to see, and ears to hear, to this day.
These wine skins, which we filled, were new; and behold, they are torn. These our garments and our sandals have become old because of the very long journey.”

I will appoint a place for my people Israel, and will plant them, that they may dwell in their own place, and be moved no more. The children of wickedness will not waste them any more, as at the first,
“Yes, forty years you sustained them in the wilderness. They lacked nothing. Their clothes didn’t grow old, and their feet didn’t swell.
though I am decaying like a rotten thing,
They spend their days in prosperity.
When I kept silence, my bones wasted away through my groaning all day long.
But God will redeem my soul from the power of Sheol,‡ Sheol is the place of the dead.
Behold, the Lord Yahweh will help me!
Lift up your eyes to the heavens,
They will not build and another inhabit.
He has made my flesh and my skin old.
